short: Austerity, the Scottish referendum, and the Brexit vote that ended his career.
full:
David Cameron formed the first British peacetime coalition since the 1930s in May 2010, governing with Nick Clegg's Liberal Democrats. The programme was deficit reduction: departmental budgets cut sharply, welfare capped, public sector pay frozen. He also legalised same-sex marriage in England and Wales in 2013, with more Labour votes than Conservative ones, and intervened in Libya in 2011.

He conceded a Scottish independence referendum, won in September 2014 by 55 to 45 per cent, then promised a referendum on European Union membership to see off UKIP and his own backbenchers. Winning an outright majority in 2015 obliged him to hold it. On 23 June 2016 the country voted to leave by 52 to 48 on a turnout of 72 per cent, and he announced his resignation the next morning, leaving office on 13 July after six years and two months.
